In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the human cerebral cortex using the magnetoencephalograhy (MEG) technique.
the development of an instrument to measure the magnetic fields generated by the brain.
the study of cerebral magnetic fields preceding self-paced plantar flexions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MEG shifts preceding unilateral movements of the feet are generated by tangential sources around the motor representation areas for the feet on the mesial surfaces of the contralaterally located hemispheres.
there is no evidence of any kind of a “cortical” origin of the EEG alpha rhythm, and that the evidence against the “thalamic” hypothesis is overwhelming.

the EEG and magnetic field shifts preceding foot movements reflect the activity of a large number of cortical neurons, and the shifts are generated by a tangential current source in the mesial surface area of the hemisphere around the foot motor representation area.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the MEG shifts preceding unilateral foot movements have a different polarity in frontal and parieto-occipital areas, and that the MEG shift preceding bilateral foot movements is the sum of the MEG shifts observed during unilateral foot movements at corresponding locations.
